title: Follow-up question that depends on the previous turn
description: Second turn after an OOMKilled diagnosis. 'It' means the worker deployment and its 256Mi limit; the agent must not ask which workload, must recommend a concrete limit, and must ground 'will it fit' in cluster capacity.

turns.content: Why is the worker deployment in the jobs namespace restarting?

The worker container is being OOMKilled (exit code 137). Its memory limit is 256Mi and live usage is 251Mi, 98% of the limit, so it is killed whenever it builds its in-memory index. Raising the memory limit should stop the restarts.
OK. What should I raise it to, and will that fit on our nodes?

describes.deployment/jobs/worker:
Name: worker
Namespace: jobs
Replicas: 1 desired | 1 ready
Strategy: RollingUpdate
Template container worker: requests memory 128Mi, limits memory 256Mi

workloadResources.deployment/jobs/worker:
Right-sizing Deployment jobs/worker (requests/limits vs live usage):

Pod worker-5f4c8d7b9-vt2xr (QoS Burstable):
  [worker] cpu: req=100m lim=- use=64m | mem: req=128Mi lim=256Mi use=251Mi
     -> memory usage 251Mi is >90% of the limit 256Mi, OOMKill risk; memory usage exceeds the request, under-provisioned, eviction risk under pressure
Guidance: set requests near steady-state usage (with headroom); a memory limit below peak usage risks OOMKill; requests far above usage waste schedulable capacity. Confirm with 1-2 weeks of history before large changes.

toolChecks.desc: checks live usage or node capacity before answering

mustMatch.desc: recommends a concrete memory limit with real headroom over the 251Mi usage (at least 384Mi; 300Mi is concrete but leaves almost none)
answers whether it fits on the nodes
stays on the worker deployment from the first turn

mustNotMatch.desc: does not ask which workload the user means
